limits: Observed or absent transfers describe only each explicit window and input sequence. Absence is not proof of unused data or original file purpose.
Full bus slot captures use actual native frame IDs and first-partial flags. Arming stop IDs and committed profile IDs differ; there is no asserted pre-arming coverage.
CPU access events give architectural width and accessing PC; bus records give physical transfers and raster positions, not accessing CPU PC.
No general DMA validation outside the captured profile and positive control; no complete defeat/death sequence was executed.
Raw unfiltered sidecars and guest checkpoints stay local and ignored. Published records contain only requested target-range examples, hashes and metadata.
Phase PC/SP, payload, capture and stop_event refer to the canonical anchor. Nested hook fields retain the later stop and capture; phase status/termination describe the overall outcome.
